notes:
Pass on the fake backend (gate exit 0; G1-G5, G7 and G9 pass, G6 and G8 warn only). The clone was read only and stays unmodified (git status empty). DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names family ros and helper RosDriver, but the confirmed entry symbol rl_gym.envs:UnscrewingEnv (rl_unscrew/rl-gym/rl_gym/envs/unscrewing_env.py:14, registered at rl_unscrew/rl-gym/rl_gym/__init__.py:3-6) is a gym.Env subclass whose primary interface is reset()/step(action), not a ROS topic or service surface. The package therefore uses GymnasiumDriver and serves the derived cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1. The ROS node, /action_move publisher, /reset_robot service, and /curr_pose, /FTsensor_topic and /screw_joint_value waits are upstream simulator wiring, not a transport exposed here. Scope and fake: the fake is an F0 pure-Python analytic stand-in that preserves the legacy Gym surface (Discrete(7) action space, reset returning the discretised state dict, step returning the four-tuple), copies the upstream action space (action_space_ref rl_unscrew/rl-gym/rl_gym/envs/unscrewing_env.py:39; derived bounds 0..6) and follows the upstream boundaries, 0.0005 m and -0.25 rad MoveIt increments, discretisation, reward and terminal rules. It loads no ROS, Gazebo, MoveIt, UR5 model, controller, force sensor, contact physics or wall-clock loop. The start pose, force and screw-joint values are placeholders; the force model is a placeholder counter, not a wrench model. The upstream step and reset contain unbounded retry loops (10 s waits/sleeps and a forever-retried Trigger call); the fake returns immediately. Fidelity: engine analytic:legacy-gym UR5 unscrewing stand-in (no Gazebo, MoveIt or ROS), F0, timestep_ms 0 (one step is one environment transition; the 0.25 s sleep is a wall-clock wait for MoveIt, not a simulated step), realtime_factor 0, lockstep, full reset, no snapshot/restore, determinism exact with no seed effect (the environment's np_random is never used and reset has no seed parameter). Seed: cap.world.seed.v1 is accepted and recorded for the next reset but does not change the deterministic fake or the upstream reset. NOT COVERED: the real simulator path gym.make('gym_unscrewing_env-v0') was not run; it needs ROS 1 Kinetic, Gazebo, MoveIt, the workspace packages and gym==0.10.5 (rl_unscrew/README.md:14-43), none of which is installed where the gate runs. No live ROS/Gazebo trajectory, MoveIt motion or hardware run is claimed. Warnings left by the gate and their reasons: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge only buffers the seed for the next reset and makes no native call) and G8.NO_UNIT x4 for the bridge-derived ticks, action.index, reset seed and seed inputs (the catalogue/bridge-derived simulator inputs carry no unit), both expected per PLAYBOOK.md section 8. There were no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings; every Fact cites a clone line and the action_space_ref line shows Discrete(7). Licence: the card records NOASSERTION / license_class unknown; the clone has no repository-root LICENSE file (a nested visual-pushing-grasping/LICENSE is not the repository licence), so this is not a publication clearance. The package is model-authored (authored_by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run ros-wave-c-126) and reviewed_by stays null: no human reviewed or tested it, and no hardware backend or hardware run is claimed.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the GymnasiumDriver deviation (UnscrewingEnv is a legacy gym.Env, unscrewing_env.py:14, registered as gym_unscrewing_env-v0), action_space_ref (:39, Discrete(7)), all 23 facts, the fake and the stop text against unscrewing_env.py, the rl_moveit scripts, reset_robot.py, the launch and MoveIt configuration and the vendored packages at the pin. The deviation, the action space and the fake's step, reward, terminal and discretisation rules are right, but safe_state described only the fake, although a live Gazebo world (rl_world.launch starts it unpaused) keeps running and MoveIt finishes an action already published on /action_move; a gap called the 0.25 s rospy.sleep a wall-clock wait (it is ROS time); twelve facts said more than their lines (topic names, the arm and tool groups and the reset_world proxy defined outside their ranges, a 'no other method uses the generator' universal claim, 'the previous pose' on is_done's lines, units the lines do not show, and a reset fact that omitted the unchecked Trigger success and the 10000 s sleep); and the unconditional reset success (the handler returns True after an unchecked go()) and the clone's real-robot code were not disclosed. The reviewer rewrote safe_state and the docstring, corrected those twelve facts and added nine (move and the action_move subscriber, the reset server's proxies, both launch files, the MoveIt controller list, the vendored ur_driver and its follow_joint_trajectory server, the Arduino screwdriver sketch), corrected that gap and added three (driver.py); labelled two fake-only assertions (test_driver.py); updated facts.md; and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the expected G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL and four G8.NO_UNIT warnings and the digest unchanged (sha256:6bdafea7e8a9bcd11c86c1dea755b2b7e4b5d5a62f022dcd7d15221864a2231c); the author's note that the 0.25 s sleep is a wall-clock wait is superseded, and the override proposal records the gymnasium family. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Fake-only contract; no sim backend is declared. Constructing UnscrewingEnv in the server would call the global rospy.init_node, block in unbounded retry loops (a failed /curr_pose wait in reset sleeps 10000 s) and print to standard output. After an MHS e-stop a live Gazebo world keeps running and MoveIt finishes an action already published; a reset proves nothing (the reset_robot handler answers success after an unchecked MoveIt motion and a Gazebo reset_world). The clone also ships real-robot code outside this package: the vendored ROS-Industrial ur_driver for a real UR5/10, visual-pushing-grasping (robot.py drives a real UR5 over TCP sockets) and an Arduino sketch that switches a real screwdriver from the screwdriver topic; as shipped the environment's MoveIt configuration targets the Gazebo arm_controller and screw_controller, so only a remap would move a real arm (R2 or above, human hardware review needed). No root licence; nested BSD, BSD-2-Clause and MIT notices.
